title.value: Run a coordinated multi-agent workflow in Copilot

introduction.value: A developer experiments with multi-agent setups in GitHub Copilot inside VS Code as part of their workflow.

method.value: The developer built a spec-driven, artifact-based agent team inside GitHub Copilot in VS Code, with stages for spec, architecture, planning, implementation, review, QA, security, integration, and docs. An Orchestrator agent ran the flow, enforced gates between stages, and relied on files like spec.md, acceptance.json, tasks.yaml, and status.json so sub-agents could reread state and continue across chats when context degraded.

outcome.value: They say it worked surprisingly well for larger features and small greenfield projects, gave more consistent results than single prompts, and asked useful clarification questions. It was slower end to end and had too much overhead for tiny quick fixes.

notes.value: The main catch was context loss in long Copilot sessions, so saving progress to artifacts on disk was central to making the workflow usable.

source_text.body:
Run a coordinated multi-agent workflow in Copilot
A developer experiments with multi-agent setups in GitHub Copilot inside VS Code as part of their workflow.
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
The developer built a spec-driven, artifact-based agent team inside GitHub Copilot in VS Code, with stages for spec, architecture, planning, implementation, review, QA, security, integration, and docs. An Orchestrator agent ran the flow, enforced gates between stages, and relied on files like spec.md, acceptance.json, tasks.yaml, and status.json so sub-agents could reread state and continue across chats when context degraded.
How it went
They say it worked surprisingly well for larger features and small greenfield projects, gave more consistent results than single prompts, and asked useful clarification questions. It was slower end to end and had too much overhead for tiny quick fixes.
Worth knowing
The main catch was context loss in long Copilot sessions, so saving progress to artifacts on disk was central to making the workflow usable.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
In VS Code, set up a multi-agent workflow for [task, e.g. adding a feature to my app] with separate roles: one agent to plan, one to implement, one to write tests, and one to review. Define each role's instructions in files in my repo and tell me how to run them in order. You're done when I can run the whole flow once on [small example task].
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1r7jx0b/experimenting_with_a_coordinated_multiagent
